dek: Yemen's internationally recognised government (Aden) formally demanded Iran stop arming Ansar Allah militias, withdraw its military experts and cease interfering in Yemen's internal affairs, accusing Tehran of prolonging the war and providing political/diplomatic cover for the group. The statement…
sources: Yemen Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates statement on X (via Arab News); 24 News HD; Sabq
fault_line: Is Iran running the Ansar Allah war through 21 embedded officers — or is Aden inflating the charge to justify the Saudi bombing campaign?

sections.what_happened: Yemen's internationally recognised government (Aden) formally demanded Iran stop arming Ansar Allah militias, withdraw its military experts and cease interfering in Yemen's internal affairs, accusing Tehran of prolonging the war and providing political/diplomatic cover for the group. The statement condemns an Iranian FM statement accusing Saudi Arabia of violating Yemeni sovereignty over strikes on civilian targets (Taiz market Nov 6, al-Shariyah). The ministry re-cited the Interior Ministry's Nov 3 announcement that 21 foreign experts work with the Ansar Allah -- 14 IRGC, 7 Hezbollah -- in command and control, ballistic missiles, drones, electronic warfare, component smuggling and maritime targeting, calling them 'a fully-fledged general staff'. It invoked UNSC Resolutions 2216 and 2624.
sections.what_verified: Demand: primary source is the ministry's own X statement; 1 declared-tier family carries it (Arab News, T3). 24 News HD, Sabq and Indian Messenger also carry it but have NO declared tier in the registry and do not count toward corroboration. The underlying 21-experts figure was separately carried Nov 3 by The National (T2), Jerusalem Post (T3) and Al Jazeera (T2).
sections.what_disputed: Iran denies arming or directing the Ansar Allah (FM spokesperson Baqaei, Nov 5, called EU accusations 'baseless'). Hezbollah called the experts claim 'entirely baseless' (Nov 4, via L'Orient Today). The UN Panel of Experts on Yemen (Oct 2024) confirmed Iranian/Hezbollah technical assistance, training, weapons and finance in general, but has NOT independently confirmed the specific 21-expert number or deployments. Yemen's ministry published no names or evidence for the 21.
sections.why_matters: Aden names the number: 21 — 14 IRGC, 7 Hezbollah — and demands Tehran pull them out, as Ansar Allah missiles hit Riyadh's Aramco tower. The charge Iran and Hezbollah both deny.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP -- Yemen's government formally demands Iran stop arming the Ansar Allah and withdraw its military experts; re-cites 21 experts (14 IRGC + 7 Hezbollah)

totw_analysis: Our read: Aden names the number: 21 — 14 IRGC, 7 Hezbollah — and demands Tehran pull them out, as Ansar Allah missiles hit Riyadh's Aramco tower. The charge Iran and Hezbollah both deny. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is Iran running the Ansar Allah war through 21 embedded officers — or is Aden inflating the charge to justify the Saudi bombing campaign?
